name: Aligned

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading:
Aligned Data Centers is headquartered in Dallas, Texas, led by CEO Andrew Schaap. As of this research date the company is mid-transaction: previously owned by private infrastructure funds managed by Macquarie Asset Management, it was the subject of an October 15, 2025 announcement in which the AI Infrastructure Partnership, MGX, and BlackRocks Global Infrastructure Partners agreed to acquire all its equity at an approximately $40 billion enterprise value, reported as the largest data center transaction on record, with closing expected in the first half of 2026. This entry does not confirm whether that transaction has actually closed.

The companys current site describes 87 data centers under management and future development across 51 campuses, with 6.4 gigawatts of operational and planned capacity, and states its North American operations are 100 percent load matched with renewable sources. The October 2025 press release cites a slightly different snapshot, 50 campuses and more than 5 gigawatts, both figures recorded here rather than reconciled to one number. A flagship project, Project Caprock, is described as a sustainable 540 megawatt next-generation campus in Northwest Texas.

The registry here tracks 7 Aligned facilities across three states, Illinois, Texas, and Virginia, a small subset of the companys ten named North American markets, which also include Maryland, Atlanta, Ohio, Phoenix, Salt Lake City, and Hillsboro, Oregon, plus four Latin American countries. Aligneds stated multi-gigawatt capacity and pending $40 billion ownership change make it one of the largest single transactions recorded across any operator in this registry, and its research_status here should be revisited once the AIP/MGX/GIP acquisition closes. This specific facility, recorded in this registry as Aligned Energy Data Center in Phoenix, AZ, was not individually named in the operator-level research above; its operator field was blank in the source data and is corrected here to Aligned based on the facility own name, which unambiguously identifies its operator brand. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.
profile.research_note: Operator field corrected from blank to Aligned based on the facility own name (source data left operator blank). Reused operator-level research from twoai_dc_operators row: Aligned.

profile.reading: This facility is attributed to Aligned, also known as Aligned Data Centers, whose own site confirms active operations across North America and Latin America, describing 87 data centers with 6.4 gigawatts of operational and planned capacity spread across 51 campuses. Confirmed North America markets include Northern Virginia, Chicago, Dallas, Phoenix, Salt Lake City, Maryland, Ohio, Atlanta, Hillsboro, and Abernathy, Texas, matching every state where this registry lists an Aligned facility (Virginia, Illinois, and Texas). The company emphasizes closed loop cooling to reduce water consumption, 100 percent renewable energy matching in North America, and adaptive modular design, and recently broke ground on Project Caprock, described as a sustainable 540 megawatt next generation data center campus in Northwest Texas. No founding date, headquarters address, ownership structure such as a possible Macquarie Asset Management connection, or acquisition history, and no building specific address or individual MW figures for this particular registry row, were located in available sourcing this session.

profile.ownership: In transition as of this research date. Previously owned by private infrastructure funds managed by Macquarie Asset Management and co-investors. On October 15, 2025, the AI Infrastructure Partnership (AIP), MGX, and BlackRock's Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) announced an agreement to acquire all equity in Aligned Data Centers at an approximately $40 billion enterprise value, reported as the largest data center transaction on record, with closing expected in the first half of 2026. This entry does not confirm whether that transaction has closed.
profile.leadership: CEO Andrew Schaap and existing leadership team retained through the announced transaction, per the press release
profile.research_note: Operator homepage did not state a founding year; press release confirms HQ as Dallas, TX. Homepage and press release give slightly different current portfolio figures (87 data centers/51 campuses/6.4 GW on the homepage vs 50 campuses/5+ GW in the October 2025 acquisition press release), both recorded rather than picking one, likely reflecting different snapshot dates.
